chapter: Early life and New Orleans arrival
title: New York winters and the move to New Orleans
summary: Carew recalls hearing music and vaudeville in New York, his acrobat ambition, and how he came to New Orleans in 1904.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Before I went to New York, yes. But I kept it up there. I, I, I bought music there. I used to go down to Segal Cooper's was a very big popular department store then. And I'd listen to the demonstrations there and buy music then. And, uh. Did you hear any ragtime players in New York? No. Any of you recall? No, no, not, none in particular. They, they played, of course, they demonstrated the music at the, at the stores, played it there. But, uh, somehow or other, uh, they didn't have those ragtime concerts, uh, or contests, rather. It may have been early, actually. They came along. Well, they came along. You see, I was there about, uh, six months in the winter. I should have heard them. I used to go to Tony Pastures and to Keith's on 14th Street and Keith's, uh, Keith's 23rd Street and, uh, Proctor's, rather. Proctor's 23rd. There were three or four vaudeville theaters. I was very strong on, on vaudeville then. My ambition was to get into vaudeville as an acrobat. I had a partner that, uh, we used to practice acrobatics together. So I went down, we were going to New York and join a show or do something. I went down and got a job. I, I did it twice. I went down there and worked six months, two winters, 1900, let's see, 1901 into two, then worked the fall into three. Three, three, three and four, that's about it. And, uh, then I got back to, to Grand Rapids and my, uh, mother went down to, uh, to Mississippi, Mississippi City. My grandparents lived. And my mother went down there to visit, uh, 1904 early in the year. And I, uh, I quit the job I had in Grand Rapids and went down there to make a visit. And, uh, while I was there, I got the idea I wanted to go to New Orleans. I got a job in Gulfport for three months first though. And in September of 1904, I got a job in New Orleans and went there.

All right. That, that, that gives a pretty good background as, as to, uh, how you, uh, happened to notice the music that you were listening to. Now, uh, certainly, uh, people like Sushan tell the story from the standpoint of a participant. And apparently he was alert to, uh, the changes that were occurring from, uh, year to year in those early years. And I, I think that, uh, your stories might very well corroborate the many things he tells. Uh, you mentioned baby seals in vaudeville. Uh, there were an awful lot of, uh, minstrel acts and coon acts and so forth available.
